revision_summary: Overall a solid, well-grounded analysis with a correctly supported outcome dispute (callback, not booked appointment) and defensible bill-anchor coaching priority. Two fixes needed on rerun: (1) Schema misuse — script_coverage lists a 'military' verify item that does not exist anywhere in the Ion schema's verify.items; remove it or replace with a real skipped field (residence_length was skipped and never mentioned, and should be added instead). Also normalize 'interest_question' to the canonical schema id verify.interest_in_solar for consistency with interest_reason_audit. (2) Reconsider the empathy_miss classification at 03:30 — the 'I'm handicapped' comment was offered casually as a scheduling justification in the same breath as agreeing to the callback, not as a weighty unprompted disclosure comparable to the schema's exemplars (Tanya's scam story, James's health situation). Either downgrade this to a minor/optional note rather than a coaching_implication-bearing classification, or explicitly justify why a brief logistical mention meets the bar of 'trust gift' per coaching_philosophy.empathy_on_vulnerability_disclosure. Additionally, strengthen the intro_legitimacy_omission cherry-pick by incorporating the rep's actual follow-up context at 00:35 ('I just work with my design team...to see if it's gonna be a good savings idea') and the transparent Google Maps narration at 01:00 — both undercut the claim that the rep did nothing to reinforce legitimacy after the customer's skepticism, and should inform a firmer strategic-vs-reactive call rather than leaving both hypotheses open-ended.
